text:
maya: kicking off a focused replaybench for a mixed-priority production-like mix (chat sessions interleaved with short embedding calls). trying to reproduce the 95/99 tail blips we saw in the Friday run. config below.

alex: copying. did you keep the same kernel selector build as prod? we changed heuristics last week.

maya: yes same image as prod (runtime:stable-2026-03), kernel-picker flags = default. KV cache warmup enabled. seed for RNG is 42.

ops-bot: job started -> replaybench/1968001111 (nodes=8, workers=32, duration=10m) :rocket:

sanjay: quick note: I see a pattern where short-sequence embedding requests get assigned to the int8 matmul path and those calls are very chatty — contention goes up under concurrent batches. maybe kernel heuristics are overfitting sequence length threshold.

kevin: hmm that's plausible. the new picker uses median sequence length from the route histogram, not per-request shape. with mixed workloads the median drifts.

maya: attaching the harness snippet we used:
```
replay_config:
  replay_source: s3://replays/mixed_priority/2026-03-12.json
  concurrency: 140
  workers_per_node: 4
  warmup: true
  kv_priming: prefix_cache
  deterministic_timing: true
  seed: 42
```

alex: did you also run the synthetic baseline (all-chat, same qps) for apples-to-apples?

maya: yes. synthetic chat baseline tail is fine. problem shows up only in mixed replay where embeddings (~50 token) are interleaved.

sanjay: I ran perf counters on a repro pod. key outputs:
```
mutex_calls: +3.2x on int8 path
L3_misses: +18% when embedding bursts hit
cpu_stall_cycles: +12%
kv_hit_ratio: 0.84 (after priming)
```
Appears to be lock contention inside the int8 GEMM wrapper when batch shapes are tiny.

tara: did batching heuristics collapse batches because of many tiny requests? we have the aggregator set to wait 4ms by default.

maya: aggregator wait was 2ms for this run (trying to reduce latency). bumping to 6ms improved throughput but increased p50. tradeoff visible.

kevin: action item: try per-shape kernel selection (hotfix) so embeddings never go through int8 path for seq <= 64. also test with aggregator wait=6ms and 12ms to build curve.

alex: also confirm that quantize-fallback isn't toggling at runtime. last incident had fallback thrash during scale-ups.

maya: good point — I saw a small number of dynamic-fallback events in the logs earlier: `quant-fallback:triggered=7` during the first 90s of the run.

sanjay: about autoscale: observed dedicated pool scale-up time 48s median, 78s p95. expected <20s. traces show many pods stuck in warmup stage waiting for kv priming. KV priming is serialized per-pod which is killing concurrency.

kevin: serialized priming was intentional to avoid storming our upstream datastore but we need a hybrid: concurrent priming up to N and then rate-limit. where N=3 maybe.

maya: also noticed burst credits drained after two scale-ups on that dedicated pool; after credits=0 fallback routed to hosted pool which increased tail. logs: `burst_credits: before=1200 after=0`

tara: is there a metric for reclaimed cache when pods die? if pods are frequently cycling we thrash KV and reduce overall hit ratio.

sanjay: yes we see `kv_reclaim_rate` spikes during scale events. suggestion: keep a grace-termination period to let cache checkpoint or move to shared cache layer.

maya: plan of experiments:
1) run the same replay with per-shape kernel selector change (force embeddings -> fp16 path)
2) sweep aggregator wait {2,6,12}ms and record p50/p95/p99 and cost/token
3) allow concurrent KV priming N=3 and measure scale-up latencies
4) run synthetic mixed-run (deterministic) to confirm apples-to-apples; compare with replay results in a single report

kevin: sounds good. can you add a small flamegraph link after run? that helped team before.

maya: will post results ~1.5h after job finishes. tagging @kevin @sanjay for follow-up.

ops-bot: job finished -> replaybench/1968001111 (final: p50=37ms, p95=212ms, p99=498ms, scaleup_p95=78s)

alex: thanks — big delta vs synthetic. keen to see per-shape selection impact.

sanjay: quick thumbs: this reproduces a new perf regression tied to kernel selection logic under mixed workloads. not a runtime-wide bug but a heuristics mismatch. :thumbsup:

maya: summary will land in the bench spreadsheet and I'll open a small PR with the selector change and tests.

kevin: please also add a note about burst-credit accounting in the PR (we might need to throttle scale-ups when credits low).

maya: noted. closing thread after I upload artifacts.
